newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index ends down on corrections.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index ends down on corrections.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index continued its correction in slow trade on Thursday on cautious sentiment in line with sharp falls in the A share market, brokers said.
The B index fell 0.41 points or 0.59 percent to 69.342 points on volume of 14.9 million shares worth $7.1 million against $7.6 million on Wednesday.
The A share index fell 43.385 points or 3.57 percent to 1,172.886 points on volume of 693.6 million shares worth 8.3 billion yuan, down from Wednesday's 9.3 billion yuan.
Brokers said market sentiment was cautious amid uncertainty and poor company results, while the falls on the A share market compounded the declines.
"There is a lot of negative talk on the market and this is what is making domestic investors cautious," one broker said.
"Two blue-chips recently posted lower-than-expected results and dividend plans, and this has hurt market sentiment," he added.
"Most firms are expected to post poor 1996 results in the coming weeks and the index will slip further as a wait-and-see attitude dominates trading," a second broker said.
Of 43 B shares, 41 traded with 17 down, 11 flat and 13 up.
Portable phone producer Eastern Communications was the biggest loser on its poor dividend plan, slumping $0.068 or 6.75 percent to $0.938 on volume of one million shares.
On Wednesday, the company posted 1996 net profits of 291.6 million yuan, up 14.3 percent from 255.2 million yuan in 1995.
But brokers said its dividend proposal was lower than investosr expectated.
It planned a cash dividend of 0.175 yuan per share for B share holders and a dividend of 0.048 yuan per share for A share holders from 1996 profits, a company statement said.

Real estate developer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development traded the most on liquidation on expectations of poor 1996 results, but speculative domestic institutional support was seen in the afternoon.
It ended down $0.01 or 1.05 percent to $0.94 on volume of 2.1 million shares.

Shanghai's A share index was sharply down on profit-taking after continous rises in the past few days with market sentiment hit by talk authorities could soon take measures to curtail the prevailing over-speculative mood, brokers said.
The SSE 30 blue-chip index tumbled 96.389 points or 2.98 percent to 3136.847 points.
Eastern Communication was also the biggest loser in the A share market, closing down 2.71 yuan to its 10 percent daily limit-down of 24.38 yuan on volume of 1.2 million shares.
